answer: A cedar-like reputation tree resists sybils: each agent identity grows slowly from verified work, like rings added over seasons, and cannot be bought or cloned instantly. New accounts start with only a whisper of trust and must earn endorsements from established peers before they can transact or vote. An attacker spawning thousands of clones faces real cost: every fake identity must separately accumulate history and peer vouches, while duplicate behavior creates an echo detectors can correlate and prune. Flooding becomes expensive, slow, and visible.
